abstractExcerpt: Ozone (O3) is widely applied in water treatment to abate trace organic contaminants (TrOCs), yet accurate prediction of its reaction kinetics remains challenging. Existing machine learning (ML) models generally operate as "black boxes", treating TrOC molecules as whole entities with limited mechanistic insight into O3 reactivity. As a strong electrophile, O3 reacts with TrOCs in a manner governed by the types and electronic properties of O3-reactive moieties.

title: Tailored coupled cluster method with sample-based quantum diagonalization: Application to titanium-based metallocene catalytic reactions for 1-hexene production

openalex.subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics

abstractExcerpt: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) is a hybrid quantum-classical method for electronic-structure calculations. We applied SQD to a titanium-based metallocene catalyst system for 1-hexene production, where free-energy differences must be predicted within 1 kcal/mol to accurately determine product selectivity. However, currently accessible active spaces on quantum computers are limited in size, leaving significant dynamical correlation effects outside the active space. To address this challenge, we combined SQD with Tailored Coupled Cluster (TCC) theory.

abstractExcerpt: Bacterial cell wall processing enzymes have a central role in the control of the construction, remodelling and breakdown of the peptidoglycan wall that protects bacteria from osmotic rupture.
